The US government announced yesterday that it has updated its list of banned foreign-made products to include "advanced robotic devices," and today a Federal Communications Commission (FCC) spokesperson confirmed that the ban also applies to robot vacuums.

The robot vacuum ban affects Roomba, Roborock, and other major brands—but you can still keep using your existing products

When the Trump administration announced a ban on "advanced robotic devices" entering the US yesterday, headlines focused on humanoid robots. But espionage doesn't require legs—neither does the FCC's robot ban. Katie Gorscak, the FCC's media relations director, confirmed to The Verge that robot vacuums are also covered by the ban.

The FCC considers advanced robotic devices to pose a national security risk. That same logic applies to products most people would consider harmless, such as robot vacuums, robot lawn mowers, and more.

Unless a device is explicitly approved, or is made in the US, it cannot be sold in the country.

The ban hits the robot vacuum market especially hard, as major brands including Roomba, Roborock, and Ecovacs are all Chinese-owned companies.

If you're using one of those products, you can keep on using it today just fine—the FCC isn't going to show up at your door to confiscate your Roomba.

However, depending on how the ban is enforced, the robot vacuum market could see some serious upheaval in the near term. If all of this sounds familiar, it's because it's essentially the same situation as the wireless router ban from a few months ago.

Will you continue to use your existing robot vacuum? Why or why not? Let us know in the comments.
